questions: Does the “entire bottom row is filled with blocks” condition consider only columns 1 through W, or does it also require that there are no blocks below row 1 (i.e., does it ignore rows with y = 0 which do not exist)?
When the bottom row is removed, are the remaining blocks’ positions updated immediately before the “for each remaining block” loop begins for that same time step?
In the “for each remaining block, in order from bottom to top” step, how is the ordering defined when multiple blocks share the same y‑coordinate but different x‑coordinates?

If a block moves downward into a cell that was just vacated by another block moving earlier in the same time step, is that allowed or does the moved‑into cell count as occupied for the remainder of the step?
Are blocks removed permanently after the bottom‑row removal, or can they reappear later (e.g., due to some external rule not described)?
Is the time limit of the simulation inclusive of the removal step at t = 10^{100}, i.e., should we process the removal at t = 10^{100} before answering queries with T = 10^{100}?
Are the coordinates (X_i, Y_i) given with y counted from the bottom (as described) or from the top of the grid, and does “bottom row” correspond to y = 1?

If multiple blocks occupy the same column but are separated by empty cells, does the “bottom‑to‑top” processing consider only vertical adjacency, or could horizontal movement ever occur (which is not described)?

inline_prompts: There is a grid with 10^9 rows and W columns. The cell at the x-th column from the left and the y-th row from the bottom is denoted by (x,y). There are N blocks. Each block is a 1 \times 1 square, and block i-th (1 \leq i \leq N) is located at cell (X_i,Y_i) at time 0. At times t=1,2,\dots,10^{100}, the blocks are moved according to the following rules: - If the entire bottom row is filled with blocks, then all blocks in the bottom row are removed. - For each remaining block, in order from bottom to top, perform the following: - If the block is in the bottom row, or if there is a block in the cell immediately below it, do nothing. - Otherwise, move the block one cell downward. You are given Q queries. For the j-th query (1 \leq j \leq Q), answer whether block A_j exists at time T_j. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N W X_1 Y_1 X_2 Y_2 \vdots X_N Y_N Q T_1 A_1 T_2 A_2 \vdots T_Q A_Q Output Print Q lines. The i-th line should contain Yes if block A_i exists at time T_i, and No otherwise. Constraints - 1 \leq N \leq 2 \times 10^5 - 1 \leq W \leq N - 1 \leq X_i \leq W - 1 \leq Y_i \leq 10^9 - (X_i,Y_i) \neq (X_j,Y_j) if i \neq j. - 1 \leq Q \leq 2 \times 10^5 - 1 \leq T_j \leq 10^9 - 1 \leq A_j \leq N - All input values are integers.
